description: The Snake in the Chinese zodiac: insight, poise and quiet determination, its Fire element, years from 1965 to 2025, and its San He, Liu He and Liu Chong matches.
answer: In Chinese astrology, the Snake is the sixth animal of the twelve-year cycle, with Fire as its fixed element and Yin polarity. It is traditionally associated with insight, poise and quiet determination. Your animal follows the Lunar New Year of your birth, so early-year birthdays can belong to the previous animal.

sections.heading: The Snake in Chinese astrology
paragraphs: The Snake is the sixth animal of the cycle and is usually described as wise, intuitive and composed. Its branch, Si, is linked with early summer, and its fixed element is Fire, often read in the Snake as inner intensity rather than outward blaze. People born in Snake years are often portrayed as thoughtful, elegant and private, with sharp judgment and a preference for depth over noise. The Snake is said to think before it moves and to pursue its goals with patient focus. Descriptions also mention secrecy and suspicion: a Snake may keep its plans and feelings hidden until it is sure. Many readings present it as a strategist whose calm surface conceals strong determination and a long memory.

Many readers recognise the Snake in a preference for watching before speaking, and in an ability to sense what is really going on beneath polite conversation. As a Yin animal, its power tends to be inward and concentrated rather than displayed.

sections.heading: The Snake at work
paragraphs: At work, the Snake is often described as analytical, discreet and quietly ambitious. Research, finance, law, psychology, philosophy, strategy, design and any role requiring careful judgment are commonly mentioned. A Snake tends to observe before acting, read people well and make well-timed moves. The traditional caution is secrecy and perfectionism: a Snake may keep information to itself, distrust colleagues or wait too long for ideal conditions. Readings often suggest that people born in Snake years do best in environments that value expertise and give them time to think, and that they benefit from sharing their reasoning more openly, so that others can support the plans the Snake has been developing quietly.

A Snake also tends to do well when given complex problems and the autonomy to solve them in its own time. It often dislikes noisy, chaotic workplaces and can be underestimated by colleagues who mistake its calm for indifference, until its preparation pays off.

sections.heading: The Snake in relationships
paragraphs: In relationships, the Snake is usually described as devoted, perceptive and intensely loyal, though slow to trust. A Snake may be charming and attentive, and it often wants a deep, private bond rather than a public display. Its classical allies are its San He partners, the Ox and the Rooster, and its Liu He secret friend, the Monkey, while the Pig sits opposite it in the six clashes. The common relationship friction is possessiveness or suspicion: a Snake may test a partner's loyalty or keep its own feelings hidden. Partners who are trustworthy, patient and comfortable with depth tend to find a Snake deeply committed and quietly protective.

Friendships with a Snake are usually small in number and deep in quality. It often makes an exceptionally discreet confidant and a thoughtful adviser. Trust is built slowly but tends to last, and a Snake is often protective of the few people it lets fully into its life.

sections.heading: Years of the Snake and their elements
paragraphs: Recent and upcoming years of the Snake are 1965 (Wood), 1977 (Fire), 1989 (Earth), 2001 (Metal), 2013 (Water) and 2025 (Wood). Each begins at Lunar New Year rather than on January 1, so people born in January or early February need to check the date: in 1977, for example, the Snake year began on February 18, and anyone born before that is a Fire Dragon. The element attached to each year comes from the ten-year cycle of heavenly stems, so a Wood Snake and a Fire Snake share the animal's core character but differ in flavour. Separately, the Snake always carries Fire as its fixed element and a Yin polarity, which describe the animal itself. Because the five stem elements and twelve animals line up again only every sixty years, the Earth Snake of 1989 returns in 2049. The Chinese zodiac calculator on this site applies the Lunar New Year table from 1924 to 2044 automatically.

sections.heading: Growth edges for the Snake
paragraphs: The growth edge for the Snake usually involves trust and openness. Traditional descriptions mention secrecy, jealousy, a tendency to hold grudges and caution that tips into paralysis. A Snake may also rely so much on its own judgment that it dismisses others' input. Practices that tend to help include sharing plans and feelings a little earlier than feels comfortable, giving people the benefit of the doubt in low-risk situations, and letting go of old slights deliberately. The Snake's gift is insight, the ability to see beneath appearances and act with precision. It tends to grow when that insight is shared generously, so that wisdom becomes connection rather than a private advantage.

In a Unified Reading, the Snake often adds a note of depth and discernment to the wider profile, echoing an introspective Life Path or Sun sign, or giving a more outgoing one a quieter centre. For anyone born in a Snake year, these growth notes are prompts for reflection rather than fixed traits.

faq.question: Is the Snake a good sign in Chinese astrology?
faq.answer: Every animal is described with strengths and challenges. The Snake is associated with wisdom, intuition and elegance, along with a tendency toward secrecy. No sign is considered good or bad overall.

faq.question: What is the Snake's element?
faq.answer: The Snake's fixed element is Fire. Each Snake year also has its own year element from the heavenly stems, giving combinations such as Wood Snake or Metal Snake.

faq.question: What years are the Year of the Snake?
faq.answer: Between 1924 and 2044 the Snake years are 1929, 1941, 1953, 1965, 1977, 1989, 2001, 2013, 2025 and 2037. Each starts at Lunar New Year, which falls between January 21 and February 20.

faq.question: Which animals are most compatible with the Snake?
faq.answer: Traditionally the Ox and Rooster share the Snake's San He trine and the Monkey is its Liu He secret friend. The Pig (Liu Chong) and the Tiger (Liu Hai) are the pairings readings treat as needing more care.
